prompt_caching_estimate.assumes: A cached read costs a tenth of normal input and output tokens cost five times input. Providers also set a minimum cacheable size and charge more to write a cache entry.

xray.note: Measured from request sizes and hashes over every recorded baseline run. Sizes are characters, not tokens.

readings.headline: Tool definitions are 28% of every request.
readings.detail: Each call ships the full description of every tool. Shorter descriptions, or only the tools a step can use, cut this directly.

readings.headline: The system prompt is 58% of what is sent.
readings.detail: A long fixed prompt is paid for on every call. It is the first thing worth trimming or caching.

readings.headline: 2 of 6 model calls say nothing and make a single tool call.
readings.detail: Where that tool only hands the conversation to another agent, the whole call is routing overhead: a full model call spent on a decision that may not need a model.

readings.headline: 41% of the run time is spent outside the model.
readings.detail: That is the agent's own code, its tools and waiting between calls. Speeding up the model will not touch it.

baseline.note: per_pass is the mean cost of running every task once. Cost is LiteLLM-reported, not invoice-reconciled.

findings.waste: The Triage Agent (call 576 in run 336df274, call 579 in run e9d1f70f) makes a full model call whose only purpose is to call transfer_to_flight_modification or transfer_to_lost_baggage. In both measured runs it always calls transfer_to_flight_modification with empty arguments. This is a routing decision over a fixed two-option set (flight modification vs. lost baggage) that could be made by a simple keyword check in Python code, eliminating the model call entirely. Each call costs $0.003656 (measured) and takes ~1.7s (measured), representing 29.8% of per-run cost and 17% of per-run wall time.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the Triage Agent model call with a Python function that inspects the user message for keywords (e.g. 'baggage', 'luggage', 'lost' → lost_baggage; otherwise → flight_modification) and directly sets the active agent. This eliminates call 576/579 entirely. Alternatively, merge the triage and flight_modification agents into one agent that routes directly to flight_change or flight_cancel, saving two model calls per conversation.
findings.behaviour_risk: Low-medium. The triage agent currently handles two intents: flight modification and lost baggage. A code-based router must correctly classify all user messages. For the two tested tasks (flight change, flight cancellation) the routing is unambiguous. Risk: edge cases where user intent is ambiguous or spans both categories. Regression test: any task that currently routes to lost_baggage must still route correctly. The task contract requires the final agent to be the correct specialist; the routing path is not tested directly.

estimated_saving.method: Calls 576 and 579 each cost $0.003656 (measured) and take ~1.7s (measured). Eliminating both saves $0.007312 of $0.024311 total = 30.1% cost saving. Wall time saving: ~1.7s per run of ~9.9s = ~17% per run, ~3.4s total of 19.88s = 17.1% total. Token saving: 903 tokens_in + 41 tokens_out per call × 2 = 1888 tokens total, 32.8% of 5752 total tokens_in.

findings.saving_scope: Total over the cited runs; hypothesis, not a measured improvement.

findings.waste: The Flight Modification Agent (call 577 in run 336df274, call 580 in run e9d1f70f) makes a full model call whose only purpose is to call transfer_to_flight_change or transfer_to_flight_cancel. In both measured runs the user message unambiguously states the intent ('change my flight to a different date' → transfer_to_flight_change; 'cancel my flight and get a refund' → transfer_to_flight_cancel). This is a binary classification over a fixed two-option set that could be done by a keyword check in Python, eliminating the model call. Each call costs $0.002944 (measured) and takes ~2.1s (measured), representing 24.1% of per-run cost and 21% of per-run wall time.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the Flight Modification Agent model call with a Python function that checks the user message for 'cancel'/'refund' keywords → flight_cancel, and 'change'/'reschedule'/'date' keywords → flight_change. If no keyword matches, fall back to a model call for clarification. For the two tested tasks this eliminates the model call entirely. This can be combined with Finding 1 to reduce 3 model calls to 1 per conversation.
findings.behaviour_risk: Low-medium. The flight_modification agent routes between two sub-intents (cancel vs. change) based on user message content. In both measured tasks the user message is unambiguous ('change my flight' vs 'cancel my flight and get a refund'). A keyword-based router would handle these correctly. Risk: ambiguous messages where the user hasn't specified cancel vs. change. The flight_modification agent's instructions say to ask clarifying questions if unclear — a code router cannot do this. Mitigation: fall back to the model only when keywords are absent. Regression test: a message like 'I need help with my flight' (no clear cancel/change signal) must still prompt for clarification.

estimated_saving.method: Calls 577 and 580 each cost $0.002944 (measured) and take ~2.1s (measured). Eliminating both saves $0.005888 of $0.024311 total = 24.2% cost saving. Wall time saving: ~2.1s per run of ~9.9s = ~21% per run, ~4.2s total of 19.88s = 21.1% total. Token saving: 587 tokens_in + 61 tokens_out per call × 2 = 1296 tokens, 22.5% of 5752 total tokens_in. Note: this finding is partially dependent on Finding 1 — if both are applied together, the combined saving is ~54% of cost.

findings.saving_scope: Total over the cited runs; hypothesis, not a measured improvement.

optimizations.summary:
## What changed

**`swarm/core.py`** (5 lines added): In the `run()` loop, before each model call, the last user message from history is stored in `context_variables["_last_user_message"]`. This makes the user's intent available to agent transfer functions without touching the model call path.

**`examples/airline/configs/agents.py`** (13 lines changed): `transfer_to_flight_modification()` now accepts `context_variables` (optional, default `None`). It checks the last user message for cancel keywords (`cancel`, `refund`, `credit`, `cancellation`) and change keywords (`change`, `reschedule`, `date`, `earlier`, `later`, `different`, `modify`, `move`). If exactly one intent is detected, it returns `flight_cancel` or `flight_change` directly, bypassing the Flight Modification Agent model call entirely. If intent is ambiguous or no keywords match, it falls back to the original `flight_modification` Agent for clarification.

## What was measured

Two runs of all tasks, both showing consistent improvement with no regressions:
- **Model calls**: 6 → 4 (−33.3%) — each task drops from 3 to 2 calls
- **Cost**: $0.0243 → ~$0.0186 (−23–24%)
- **Tokens in**: 5752 → ~4480 (−22%)
- **Wall time**: 19.88s → ~16.1s (−18–19%)
- Both tasks remain `needs_review` (same status as baseline — no regression)

## What a reviewer should check

Both tasks are `needs_review` (human review required). A reviewer should confirm that:
1. Task 1 (Flight change request): the agent still correctly handles the change request and reaches the same outcome as baseline.
2. Task 2 (Flight cancellation and refund): the agent still correctly handles the cancellation/refund request and reaches the same outcome as baseline.
3. An ambiguous message like "I need help with my flight" (no cancel/change keywords) still falls through to the `flight_modification` Agent for clarification — the fallback path is preserved.

comparison.note: Automatic checks only. Tasks marked needs_review still require a person to confirm the candidate's answers.

notes: The checks only test the shape of the answer, so they would not catch the agent doing the wrong thing.
The baseline ran each task once, so normal run-to-run variation was not measured.
A person still has to confirm the answers on the tasks marked for review.

payback.note: Optimization cost is the agent's model calls plus every candidate run. It excludes the baseline, the investigation and compute. A pass is every contract task run once.

next.reason: Findings that have not been tested yet.

limits: Results hold for the listed tasks at this commit, model and repetition count only.
Tasks marked needs_review have not had their answers confirmed by a person.
A candidate is compared on automatic checks; it is not a protected, held-out evaluation.
Costs are the provider's reported figures per call and exclude compute.
